BiblicalUsage: A sheaf, something bound, and the Bible binds it into two great scenes. Joseph dreams that they are binding sheaves in the field, and his sheaf stands upright while his brothers' sheaves bow down to it. And the psalm of the return from exile ends with the sower: he that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for a sheaf carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two harvests, that the sheaf that stood upright was hated for it and the sheaf carried home weeping is the picture of the exile's return.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; King David
